name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,341

entries.clue: Head of gardening with permits for wooden frame (7)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of gardening
permits = allows, as verbs

annotation.surface: A gardener gets planning permission to put up a wooden trellis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wooden frame' sounds like garden joinery, a trellis or cold frame; the frame is the grim one used for hanging.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the structure for hanging people is a timber frame of posts and crossbeam.

blocks.note: a span of about 25-30 years, parent to child
the act of producing something, such as electricity

annotation.walkthrough: Two words, two unrelated senses of GENERATION: a span of time and the act of producing something.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are plain senses: a generation is a span of years between parent and child, and generation is the producing of power or ideas.

entries.clue: Brand left on first murder victim (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it

blocks.note: L = left
in Genesis, Abel is killed by his brother Cain, the first murder

annotation.surface: A mark left branded on the body of the first murder victim.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a crime scene; 'Brand' is the noun, a trade name, not a burn mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the commercial sense: a record label or fashion label is the brand goods are sold under.

indicatorNotes.following: the attendant comes after the old boy

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil of a school
an attendant is a servant

annotation.surface: A dutiful servant trails after an elderly gentleman.
annotation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school, usually shortened to OB.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone quick to notice what is going on around them.

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing sizes
lorry is the British word for a truck

annotation.surface: Someone is knocked down by a small lorry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit' reads as a noun or present tense; here it is the past tense, which is what STRUCK needs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: strike and hit mean the same, and struck is strike's past form.

blocks.note: a noun here: the fastening on a door or window
a strand or tress, as in a curl kept as a keepsake

annotation.surface: Someone grabs a strand of hair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like a verb acting on the hair, but it is a noun: the fastening on a door.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated nouns spelt alike: the fastening that secures a door, and a strand of hair.

indicatorNotes.turned over: flipping the word makes it read backwards

blocks.note: a pal is a friend

annotation.surface: A friend knocks their drink over.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface spills a glass; the drinking is done the way a cat takes milk.
annotation.definitionFit: A narrower sense of drink: lapping is drinking by scooping liquid up with the tongue, as a cat does.

entries.clue: Engineer directs final bit of film (7)

indicatorNotes.Engineer: to engineer something is to construct or rearrange it

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A sound engineer directs the closing scene of a movie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun, the film's sound engineer; it is a verb telling you to rebuild DIRECTS.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the list of cast and crew rolls at the very end of a film.

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals: every other one

blocks.note: letters 1, 3 and 5 of nEaRbY

annotation.surface: Someone named Nick often lives close at hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is the British slang verb for steal or arrest.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for seizing, whether stealing something or arresting someone; nick is chiefly British.

blocks.note: raced = sped; it goes around the net
a net is a trap

annotation.surface: Someone rushed to keep a net tied down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Net' tempts as a fishing net to be tied down; it is a snare, the thing that catches, and 'to keep' is the instruction to wrap around it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by method: buckling something with a strap is one way of fastening it.

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are arranged badly and must be put right

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A sound belief comes to a sorry end.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a small contradiction: a belief called tenable that still ends badly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tenable comes from holding a position, and a position you can hold is one you can defend.

blocks.note: a noun here: the straight stick marked in inches or centimetres
a monarch, emperor or other sovereign

annotation.surface: Taking the measure of a nation's leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Measure' reads as a verb; it is the noun, the tool you measure with.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the marked stick used for measuring, and the one who rules a country.

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
mine = belonging to me

annotation.surface: Someone boasts that the red car is theirs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a proud owner pointing at a red car; the colour is the answer and the car is only wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: carmine is one particular shade of red, deep and crimson.

blocks.note: to rein in is to control, as with a horse
might = force, power

annotation.surface: Keeping control could make things stronger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Might' reads as the helping verb; it is the noun meaning power.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: builders add steel to concrete to make it stronger.

indicatorNotes.almost: not quite the whole word: drop its last letter

blocks.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
cut = AXE, less its last letter

annotation.surface: A god very nearly wounds someone in the chest.
annotation.walkthrough: Thor, who swings a hammer, fits a surface about cutting.
annotation.definitionFit: The anatomical term for the chest, the part of the body between neck and abdomen.

blocks.note: an adjective here, as in the first night of a play
a chance, such as a vacancy for a job

annotation.surface: A first chance at something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First' works as an adjective: an opening night is the first night.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the adjective for what comes first, as in opening night, and the noun for a chance or vacancy.

entries.clue: Time publication for paper with little substance (6)

blocks.note: T = time
an issue is one publication of a magazine

annotation.surface: A jibe that an issue of Time magazine is a flimsy, lightweight paper.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads Time as the magazine and 'paper' as a newspaper; the paper is literal, thin tissue paper.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: tissue paper is so thin it has almost no substance, while the surface hints at thin content.

indicatorNotes.featuring: the phrase features the answer inside it

blocks.note: gumMY STICker

annotation.surface: A sticky label with a fortune-teller printed on it.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the word break between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: both claim insight beyond the ordinary senses, as a fortune-teller does.

entries.clue: Clearly too accepting of leader of tribe (7)

indicatorNotes.accepting: OVERLY accepts a letter into itself
indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: too = overly, excessively; it goes around the T
first letter of tribe

annotation.surface: Someone is plainly too willing to follow a tribal chief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Accepting' reads as being too tolerant of a chief; it is the container instruction, and 'Clearly' at the front is the definition, an adverb like the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: done in the open, where everyone can see it clearly.

indicatorNotes.initially: take the initial, the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Fools
waste = loss, as in a loss of time

annotation.surface: Only fools throw away their dental floss at first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Waste' reads as a verb in the surface; it is the noun, a loss.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the thread you pull between your teeth cleans where a brush cannot reach.

indicatorNotes.without leader: a word without its leader has lost the letter that heads it

blocks.note: mitigate = SOFTEN, minus its first letter S

annotation.surface: Advice to ease things often when nobody is in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: SOFTEN loses its S; the leader in the surface sounds like a person in charge.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: many times, at short intervals.

entries.clue: One filming Purge returned holding right page (8)

indicatorNotes.returned: sent back, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: purge = RID, read backwards
the recto is the right-hand page of an open book

annotation.surface: Someone shooting the horror film The Purge.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make Purge look like the film being shot, so 'One filming Purge' seems to run together; the definition stops at 'One filming' and purge is a plain verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by role: the person in charge of shooting a film.

entries.clue: Heads of European nations determined objective (3)

indicatorNotes.Heads of: the head of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of European, Nations, Determined

annotation.surface: European leaders settle on a shared goal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heads of European nations' reads as political leaders; it means the first letters of the next three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for an aim, as in 'the end justifies the means'.

blocks.note: a keyboard key, the one that jumps to the next field
the American word for a running bill, as at a bar

annotation.surface: A crucial piece of legislation before Congress.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Key bill' an important law in Washington; 'in Washington' only marks the American sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a keyboard key, and in American English the bill you run up at a bar or restaurant.

entries.clue: Old silver cot with head missing (4)

indicatorNotes.with head missing: a word with its head missing has lost the letter at its top

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
cot = BED, minus its first letter

annotation.surface: An antique silver cot that has lost its headboard.
annotation.walkthrough: The head missing from the cot sounds like a broken headboard; it is the B of BED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for elderly, as in an aged relative; silver also hints at grey hair.

indicatorNotes.empty: empty the word of its middle, leaving its outer letters

blocks.note: C = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
a lean year is an unproductive one
SubmarinE with its middle removed

annotation.surface: A submarine, caught out and emptied, gets washed down.
annotation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scoring, where a batsman out caught is marked c.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with a sense of thorough or ritual washing.
